title: HyperMLP: An Integrated Perspective for Sequence Modeling
claim: A sequence-modeling head can be recast as a dynamic two-layer MLP whose weights come from context, which unifies attention variants and motivates a new design.
layout: 6 panels: top two wide parameterization diagrams, bottom four MLP views left-to-right
description: A dense multi-panel figure. The top row has two wide panels. Panel (a) shows attention baselines as a dynamic MLP. Colored matrices (orange, green, purple, blue) are combined through factorized and low-rank parameterization, then pass through an activation (softmax/ReLU) to give a hidden attention-score vector and an output. Colored callout boxes list variants such as RoPE, GLA and Toeplitz. Panel (b) shows the same layout for HyperMLP/HyperGLU, with extra diagonal-plus-low-rank sequence-mixing matrices and a Norm/ReLU/GLU gating block. The bottom row has four network-style diagrams. (c) is a fixed 2-layer ReLU MLP. (d) is ReLU attention as a dynamic MLP with context-instantiated memory. (e) is linearized attention as a dynamic linear map. (f) is HyperMLP with sequence and feature mixing, shown with faded overlays and highlighted curved arrows. Each bottom panel has a formula underneath and dashed separators between panels. Green, blue and orange nodes carry the meaning.
caption: The integrated attention-as-MLP view: dynamic two-layer MLPs, memory instantiation, and HyperMLP.
abstract: Self-attention is often viewed as probabilistic query-key lookup, motivating designs that preserve normalized attention scores and fixed positional semantics. We advocate a simpler and more unified perspective: an autoregressive attention head can be viewed as a dynamic two-layer MLP whose weights are instantiated from the context history. From this view, attention scores form an ever-growing hidden representation, and standard MLP activations such as ReLU or GLU naturally implement input-conditioned selection over a context-dependent memory pool rather than a probability distribution. Based on this formulation, we introduce HyperMLP and HyperGLU, which learn dynamic mixing in both feature space and sequence space, using a reverse-offset (lag) layout to align temporal mixing with autoregressive semantics. We provide theoretical characterizations of the expressivity and implications of this structure, and empirically show that HyperMLP/HyperGLU consistently outperform strong softmax-attention baselines under matched parameter budgets.
